answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post jobs or claim rewards, with influence capped by the amount and age of the lock. Splitting one stake across a hundred accounts then creates no extra weight, while each account still adds setup overhead. A protocol can slash the bond for provable fraud, making a Sybil campaign risk real capital and time rather than merely minting names; gale, basalt, and copper could be accepted tokens only if they meet the same scarcity and slashing rules.
